ca_p_t_barnum_wall.blurb: P.T. Barnum Wall is a sport crag in the Inner Gorge of the Owens River Gorge, in the Eastern Sierra near Bishop. The twenty bolted lines here are long and sustained, and the grades start around 5.10 then climb quickly: most sit in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a handful of 5.13s. That makes it a wall for upper-intermediate and strong climbers rather than beginners. The pink-varnished volcanic rock is quite featured, and the wall gets sun early and goes into shade later in the day, which helps on warm afternoons. It is a quiet, secluded corner of the gorge, usually far less busy than the better-known roadside crags, and it rewards good endurance.

ca_plum_valley.blurb: Plum Valley is a small, out-of-the-way bouldering area in the Lassen region of northeast California, up on the Hat Creek Rim at roughly 4,700 feet. About twenty problems sit on solid volcanic rock at the foot of a talus slope, tucked among trees near a reservoir bed that may be dry. The spread is wide: a good number of easy lines in the V0 to V3 range with flat landings, a middle tier of moderates, and a few hard problems up to about V8. Some landings have been built up and a little trail work done, and more boulders are scattered through the talus and under the rim. A pleasant spot for a quiet day of climbing.

ca_get_carter_boulder.blurb: Get Carter Boulder is a single large boulder on the west side of Buttermilk Country, in the Bishop area of the Eastern Sierra. It stands right beside the dirt road, so the walk is almost nothing. Around twenty problems cover a very broad range, from easy cracks and corners at V0 to V3 up through the V6 and V7 classics, then on to a cluster of V8 to V12 testpieces for strong boulderers. The granodiorite offers finger cracks, steep overhangs and dynamic moves. It is best from late fall into spring when temperatures are cool; bring two crash pads and a spotter for the taller lines.
ca_get_carter_boulder.parking_note: Park in the Birthday Boulders lot, bear right where the road forks and walk it downhill; the boulder sits right next to the road.

ca_zippy_rock.blurb: Zippy Rock is a rounded granite formation in the Stirrup Tank section of Joshua Tree National Park, in the Pinto Basin on the quieter east side of the park. Around twenty routes are recorded, mostly traditional crack and flake lines, with a few bolted and top-rope options. Difficulty runs from very easy up to about 5.11, and the largest group of lines sits around 5.10, so it suits climbers comfortable placing their own gear. Expect typical Joshua Tree monzogranite: coarse, grippy and sometimes unnerving on faces. Stirrup Tank sees far fewer people than the famous areas near Hidden Valley, though quality varies from route to route.

ca_tower_of_babel_2.blurb: Tower of Babel is a conglomerate dome in Texas Canyon, in the Angeles National Forest between Santa Clarita and Agua Dulce. The west side is a steep, knobby wall of roughly 180 feet with a bulging lower section, then plenty of pockets and cobbles higher up; seen from the east it looks low-angled and slabby. Most of the twenty routes are bolted, with a few trad lines and one top-rope, and difficulty spans from 5.2 up to about 5.11, so there is something for newer and experienced climbers. It tends to be quiet. The conglomerate is fragile after rain, so wait for it to dry before climbing.

ca_lowenbrau_pinnacle.blurb: Lowenbrau Pinnacle is the tallest formation in McCain Valley, a desert climbing area in southern San Diego County. It offers a handful of two-pitch leads on textured granite, a mix of traditional cracks, face routes and flakes, with some bolted lines and a few aid climbs. Roped grades run from about 5.7 to the low 5.13s, with most routes between 5.7 and 5.11, so it works for moderate leaders as well as hard climbers. The valley is known for light crowds, and the summit gives wide views across the surrounding desert. A good choice when you want longer climbs than the valley's boulders and short crags provide.
